MW_GAMES_entry.name: Arrhythmix
MW_GAMES_entry.tagline: One ECG, six diagnoses, three tries. Read the rhythm.
MW_GAMES_entry.quip: Squiggles in, diagnosis out. Calipers optional.
MW_GAMES_entry.helpQuip: “Sinus rhythm” is not a personality. Read the strip.
help: Read the short case and the ECG, then pick the diagnosis from six options.
You get three tries. Each wrong pick unlocks a hint.
Tap Zoom (or the ECG) to enlarge it. Standard paper: 25 mm/s and 10 mm/mV, so one small square is 40 ms and 0.1 mV.
Easy and Medium days show a lead II rhythm strip. Hard and Genius days show a 12-lead.
After you finish, Key features highlights what to look for on the trace.
Difficulty rises through the week: Easy Mon-Tue, Medium Wed-Thu, Hard Fri-Sat, Genius Sun.
A new ECG arrives at midnight, Sydney time. Past ECGs live in the archive.

arrhythmix: Arrhythmix is a daily ECG quiz. Each day brings a short fictional case and an ECG drawn on standard ECG paper. Pick the diagnosis from six options in three tries; wrong picks unlock hints, and every answer comes with the key features highlighted on the trace and a teaching pearl.
Students, nurses, paramedics, doctors and anyone learning ECGs. Monday’s rhythm strips are gentle; Sunday’s 12-leads are not.
No. Every trace is computer-generated from parameters to show the textbook features, and every case is fictional. General education, not medical advice.

arrhythmix.name: Riff
cheer: My heart skipped a beat. The good kind.
